items.note: The plan states the eight-row schedule, the net change (JV+RG)x independent of the scratch values, the central coefficients |S∩T| mod 2 and (|S∩T|-1)/2 cancelled by the side wires, and the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) with every auxiliary wire restored, as in the proof at 741-765. It never gives h=100, the neighbour relations or the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-783), but these belong to the construction rather than to the lemma's proof.

It states the invariant (stored array = D_v applied to the logical array), that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on every role, exactly as at 804-825.

These are correct: the nondegenerate nested labels built from triple indicators with <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1, the only decreasing edges being center 3->4 with loss h, L=Ich, the signed sum Wm-2N, the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L, and L/N=100/539 and 101/539. The derivation omits the stage-transition and gate-label tables (eq:motif-labels), the residual table that checks comparability edge by edge (1013-1064), and the orthonormal bases of binary residuals (1073-1102).

s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m is stated correctly, with the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one. The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m is only referred to as 'the endpoint condition' (S1.1.6.3). The plan never gives the assignment of P_U to gates and sinks, why P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U (1158-1161), or the computation P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m (1169-1171).

It has the right phase frames C_U=H^{⊗m}diag(i^{wt(P_U x)})H^{⊗m}, the key fact that weight is additive mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, and one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector. Missing: the count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and the endpoint argument (Z_{a,k} corrections and the i^{27k} scalar on the X_a->Y_a route, negating the X outputs) that gives C^{⊗m} on every role (1273-1314).

For the bit network the chain is complete and correct: L_b/N<1/2, deficit N-2L_b>0, eta_b=339/22587335000000>20*2^-50, then m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), so s/W<m^tau. The step log m<20 behind the first inequality is only implicit. For the complex network only L_c/N=101/539 is given: s_c<W_c m, eta_c=73/19906842167500 and s_c/W_c<m^sigma are never derived, although S2.3.5 uses a=s/W<=m^sigma.

The plan uses linear-cost controlled shifts, single-digit operations and the cyclic row split into W streams. It never states the lemmas' content, such as the condition that the offset be computable in b^{O(1)} time or the list of O(V) operations.

The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 (topmost row, rightmost pivot), the O(V) lower-triangular transformations, the order of the steps, and the sequence D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j all follow 1375-1447. The statement leaves q unspecified, but the lemma requires a fixed odd prime avoiding every denominator and every diagonal numerator of the factors (1397, 1413-1423).

Every step of the proof appears: the base case, the cyclic split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_M frames giving Phi_{I_m} on every row, the interchange D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D, s calls, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum, and the O(V) fixed-tape parking schedule.

It follows the paper's three moves: the top rho=O(log e) digits supply rows, the remaining width is split in base m with cost O(V)Σa_j m^{jτ}, and binary chunks are padded to [q^e]. It omits the zero-row padding to R'=W^k⌈R/W^k⌉ (1684-1690), which gives the divisibility the power-width proposition needs. S1.2 only claims 'at least W^k rows'.

It gives: residual bases are conjugated into coordinate position by GL(m,F_2) row additions on whole slots; a node makes exactly s_c child calls on f=e/m axes; inverse children follow from (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f}C^{⊗f}Z^{⊗f}; and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. All match 1835-1940.

Faithful: the eight conditional ±1 additions and their parity cycles, the guard interval [10,2^{K-1}-11], delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, the chunk swaps around the controlled rotations, the repair by sorting only extracted records, and the full time bound.

Faithful: node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), rows from the first q_0 chunks with range at least W^{k_0}, children of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the internal and leaf sums, and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}).

It states the O(Vd^{lambda'}) cost with exact evaluation and one truncation, the guard width Delta=⌈C_0 d^{C_1}⌉=o(p) from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, the depth-to-width induction, and the final error below sqrt2 2^-p. The proof assembles these as the paper does.

Faithful: character cancellation by the halving shift, decimation in frequency giving B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, grouped rounds, layout moves costing O(TpdK) and O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}) layer rounds, and the error sqrt2 ell 2^-p.
Faithful: B_0=2^{4p}, four products, |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2, centred residues with carry in {0,1}, negacyclic reduction, a shift by p+ell, and O(rp log(rp)) cost.

It gives the retained LB order, the normalization M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)/r)=(f*g)/(rM), permutation-equivariance of the pointwise product, the error 3delta+eta scaled by M, and the cost, all as in the proof.

Correct: the identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, the Neumann inversion of N=CTD, the normalizations, the retained permutations, the tensor form RF_s=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A, and the line-map cost. The permutations (P_s u)_j=u_{tj}, (P_t v)_k=v_{-sk} are never defined. The tensor proof's axis exposure by chunk swaps, O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)), and its valid-set/error dp^2 bookkeeping (3836-3889) are missing.

Both identities and their proofs (coefficient expansion, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+, the normalized convolution rule) follow 3938-3983. The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i Σ s_i j_i^2/t_i) itself is never written, and the plan does not say that RF_s^+ is obtained by conjugation.

The exponent list, layer inequalities, sizes, alpha and gamma bounds, the prime-interval count, disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search, and no wraparound all match the paper.

It gives: the isomorphism x->Πx_i^{mu_i}, the triangular coordinates b_i=a_i+mu_i Σ_{j<i} a_j P_j, updates in the order i=d..1, rotations preserving the padding, prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, and the O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)) cost.

It gives the well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isometry, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the twist approximations, matching 4303-4377.

The source transform (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma with exact counterpart RF_s), the six-step algorithm, and the account of the two factors of S all match. The input digit scaling by 2^{-b-2} and the definition F~^+(z)=conj(F~(conj z)) are not stated.

The disk margin .701, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (3E_s+2), the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding and carries are all correct. The plan skips the intermediate error steps: E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL, the complex convolution <6TL, and the chirp transform <8TL (4582-4639), from which E_s is built.

Each table row, power and margin g_1..g_7 is correctly stated, with min g_i=2^-181=2kappa, the log p absorption and the cutoff. S7.10 gives a slightly wrong reason for the o(V) exceptional-sorting term (see errors).
S0 says the bound refutes the n log n conjecture in this model. It does not give the liminf formulation or explain why one machine with this bound suffices.

errors.says: Method: the eight-row schedule should 'first cancel the old scratch contents', then add the source's effect, then restore the scratch.
errors.paper: Rows 0-1 subtract the effect of the old scratch values on the target (J a + R c); the scratch contents themselves are not cancelled but changed by rows 2-3 and restored by rows 6-7.

errors.says: Nested labels make the cost of an edge change equal to the dimension of its orthogonal residual.
errors.paper: For the bit network, rank equals the dimension change except on the N source edges of X_a, where the matrix 2P_{U_a} has rank one but the dimension change is zero. The plan corrects this later in S1.1.4.4.

errors.says: Motivation: the row field divisible by W^k is supplied by the chunk's own high digits and a base-m decomposition.
errors.paper: The high digits give a row range R=q^{2rho}>=W^k; divisibility comes from appending zero rows until the count is R'=W^k⌈R/W^k⌉<2R.

errors.says: Setup, descriptors, prime search and the compact sorting of exceptional records are o(V) because visits are polynomial in p while r exceeds every power of p.
errors.paper: The exceptional sorting is O(V p^{A'} 2^{-K})=o(V) because K=Theta(p^{eps c}) makes 2^{-K} beat every polynomial in p, not because of r. The prime search is n^{o(1)} by a separate argument.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: power-width interchange, then arbitrary-width interchange, simultaneous layer, synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, assembly, precision, and the time table with min g_i=2kappa. The bit-network saving and its recurrence are reconstructed in detail. The chain thins in three places: the network sizes (h=100, N, m) are never given; the endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m and the complex interface's s_c<W_c m with its C^{⊗m} endpoint corrections are only alluded to, so sigma for the butterfly recursion is asserted rather than derived; and the error chain jumps from ring convolution to E_s.

steps.note: The exchanging network on triples of [h] is described (eight-row schedule, (x,y)->(-y,x), scratch restored), but h=100, the indexing of data pairs by T^3, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given. N and m appear later without definition, so the step is marked mentioned, the conservative choice.
It has the common frame commuting with a pointwise gate, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and that only endpoint frames are forced, so intermediate frames can make edges cheap.
It has nondegenerate subspace labels in an m-dimensional tensor space built from triple indicators, comparable labels on every edge, and the only decreasing edges being center 3->4, each losing h.

It states that rank equals the dimension change on every edge except the N negative source projections, whose edge matrix 2P_{U_a} has rank one. The reason that P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U is only implicit.
It has the signed sum Wm-2N, Ic decreasing edges of loss h giving L=Ich, the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
It has L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, and deficit N-2L_b>0, so s_b<W_b m.

The plan says 'the frame identity and the endpoint condition give Phi_{I_m}', the shear on every row. The identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and its source (-P_{U_a} at X_a sources, P_{U_a^perp} at Y_a sinks) are never stated, so it is marked mentioned, the conservative choice.
It has A=E_1 Pi E_2, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) per edge, and the s recursive calls at a node as the sum of edge ranks.

It has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), eta_b>20*2^-50 with m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta) so s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50, and F_k=O(e^tau). The fact log m<20 is used only implicitly.

central.summary: Seven of the nine steps are reconstructed. The plan carries the frame principle, the labels and their only loss on central wires, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, the strict saving from L/N=100/539, the factorization giving s calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. The fixed network appears without its sizes (h=100, N, m), and the endpoint identity that makes every role a shear H<-H+D is named but never stated or derived.
